questions.title: Who will succeed Brendon McCullum as permanent head coach of England's men's Test team?
questions.background: Brendon McCullum currently coaches England's men's Test cricket team.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : An official England and Wales Cricket Board appointment announcement or reliable contemporaneous reporting of that announcement. Resolution : Resolve to the first person formally appointed as McCullum's permanent successor as head coach of England's men's Test team. Interim appointments and appointments solely concerning limited-overs cricket do not count. Resolution occurs when the appointment is announced, even if the coach begins work later. Accepted Answer Format : The appointed coach's full name.

questions.title: Which DRC province will WHO identify as experiencing a surge in weekly Ebola cases in mid-September 2026?
questions.background: The Democratic Republic of Congo declared an Ebola outbreak in May 2026.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : WHO public statements about the DRC Ebola outbreak, including statements quoted in contemporaneous reputable news reporting. Resolution Window : Resolve to the province explicitly identified by WHO as experiencing surging weekly Ebola cases in its outbreak assessment publicly reported between September 10 and September 16, 2026. Accepted Answer Format : The name of the province.
questions.current_reasoning: July 7-9 Reuters/Al Jazeera reporting on the DRC government's July 8 night sitrep shows confirmed Bundibugyo Ebola cases jumped to 1,759 and deaths hit 600 (+198 cases and +94 deaths in 4 days; 51 cases and 20 deaths in 24h), with WHO DRC rep Dr. Anne Ancia warning July 7 the outbreak remains in its 'expansion phase' with ~90% ETC occupancy and mobile Mongbwalu miners seeding new areas. Crucially, the July 8 sitrep reported two positive Ebola test cases (pending confirmatory validation) in Kisangani, the 1.5M-person capital of Tshopo province—one linked to Niania (Ituri) and a second with 'no geographic link' beyond Kisangani, pointing to unlinked urban transmission in a major Congo River hub with no approved vaccine. Because an urban second wave in Kisangani is primed to surge ~9 weeks out in mid-September, we lift Tshopo sharply (0.13 -> 0.22), while keeping North Kivu slightly ahead (0.28 -> 0.24, 11/35 affected HZs, M23 governance gaps) pending lab confirmation. Ituri stays #1 (0.39 -> 0.36) amid July 9 health-worker pay protests/walkouts outside three Bunia treatment centres, Haut-Uele trims slightly (0.10 -> 0.09), and South Kivu drops to 0.04 after 44 days (two full 21-day cycles) with zero new confirmed cases since May 26 (leaving 5% tail for Kinshasa/Maniema/Bas-Uele).

questions.title: In which country outside Iran, if any, will US forces strike Iran-aligned armed groups between July 22 and July 29, 2026?
questions.background: Iran-aligned armed groups operate across several Middle Eastern countries, creating potential flashpoints for military confrontation with the United States.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : Contemporaneous reporting by Al Jazeera, supported where available by official military statements. Resolution Conditions : Identify the country outside Iran where US forces conduct strikes against Iran-aligned armed groups between July 22 and July 29, 2026, inclusive. Direct US participation in either unilateral or joint strikes qualifies; threats, proposed operations, and diplomatic support do not. Accepted Answer Format : The country's name, or “None” if no qualifying strikes occur.

ISW (July 8/9) reports IRGC Quds Force commander Esmail Ghaani is in Najaf for Khamenei's funeral and likely meeting Iraqi Shia militia leaders, while Iran's parliamentary National Security Commission floated closing the Bab-el-Mandeb Strait (July 9) and Iranian officials met Houthi representatives at the funeral. However, we keep None high (0.46 -> 0.39) alongside Iraq (0.34 -> 0.40) because neither Iraqi militias nor Houthis entered either the June 27-28 or July 7-9 exchanges, Trump reportedly told advisers he will not resume full-scale war unless US troops are killed, Maersk/Hapag-Lloyd just resumed Suez/Red Sea transit July 6-8, and July 22-29 is only an 8-day window. local_articles.snippet: July 13 - The Iran-aligned Houthi movement that controls northern Yemen accused Saudi Arabia on Monday of launching airstrikes against the international airport in Sanaa, and vowed to retaliate. Houthi military spokesperson Yahya Saree called the attacks "blatant aggression" and said they had ended a period of de-escalation in the long-running conflict. questions.title: Which country will announce a new multinational maritime coalition to protect navigation through the Red Sea, Bab al-Mandeb Strait and Gulf of Aden by August 1, 2026?
questions.background: Attacks on commercial shipping since 2023 have heightened concerns about the security of maritime trade routes through the Red Sea.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : Official government announcements or contemporaneous reporting by reputable international news organizations. Resolution Conditions : Identify the country that announces the creation of a new multinational maritime coalition between July 1 and August 1, 2026, inclusive, with a stated purpose of protecting freedom of navigation through the Red Sea, Bab al-Mandeb Strait and Gulf of Aden. Joining an existing coalition does not qualify. Accepted Answer Format : The country's common English name.
questions.current_reasoning: Existing frameworks (US Operation Prosperity Guardian, CMF/CTF 153, IMSC/Sentinel, EU Operation ASPIDES, and the UK-France Hormuz coalition announced in April-May 2026) do not qualify, so a new multinational coalition specifically targeting the Red Sea, Bab al-Mandeb Strait, and Gulf of Aden must be announced in July 2026. Saudi Arabia (leader of the Red Sea Council and heavily reliant on its Yanbu Red Sea export bypass during the Hormuz closure) and Egypt (suffering massive Suez Canal losses, current CTF 153 commander, and alarmed by Red Sea/Somaliland tensions) are the top regional candidates to unveil an Arab/littoral maritime coalition. The United States (with Secretary Rubio touring the Gulf in late June on post-war security), the United Kingdom, and France (which has a Djibouti base at Bab al-Mandeb and co-led the Hormuz coalition) are the main Western contenders, leaving 31% tail mass on UAE, Turkey, China, Israel, India, or other states.
